summary: ReDoS (CWE-1333/CWE-400) in NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber(): the pre-validation regex PATTERN_FLOAT = [+-]?[0-9]*[.]?[0-9]+(...)? has adjacent quantifiers over the digit class, so a long run of digits that ultimately fails to match backtracks in O(n^2). jackson-databind calls this method during String-to-number coercion before any length limit applies, so a single long JSON string value bound to a number type pins a CPU thread (reporter measured ~74s for a 160,000-char string).
vulnerable_feature: jackson-databind String-to-number coercion (JSON string value coerced to Float/float, Double/double, BigDecimal, or generic Number), plus JsonNode StringNode numeric coercion (asInt/asLong/asBigInteger/asFloat/asDouble/asDecimal). All of these pre-validate the text with tools.jackson.core.io.NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber(String).
trigger_conditions: App deserializes untrusted JSON (e.g. Spring MVC @RequestBody / HttpMessageConverter -> JsonMapper/ObjectReader.readValue) where the target has at least one float/double/BigDecimal/Number property, OR the app reads values off a JsonNode via asInt/asDouble/asDecimal etc.

Attacker sends that numeric field (or any string later coerced to a number) as a JSON STRING containing a long run of digits followed by a non-numeric tail, e.g. {"price":"1111...1x"} with length ~10^5-10^6.

No special Jackson feature required; default StreamReadConstraints.maxStringLength (20,000,000) does NOT bound the cost. Coercion of a bare JSON number token (not a string) does NOT hit looksLikeValidNumber, so the value must arrive as a JSON string (default ALLOW_COERCION_OF_SCALARS=true permits string->number).

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Diff core 3.1.5->3.1.7 (issue #1649): regex PATTERN_FLOAT/PATTERN_FLOAT_TRAILING_DOT removed and replaced by a hand-rolled single-pass scan. desc derived from source signature 'public static boolean looksLikeValidNumber(final String s)'. Local benchmark of the exact 3.1.5 regex: 5k/10k/20k/40k digit+'x' strings = 121/316/1267/4595 ms (quadratic).

StdDeserializer.java:1087 calls NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber(text) on the primitive-float String path. (Note: the double-primitive path _parseDoublePrimitive got the same pre-validation ADDED only in 3.1.7, see #6179.)
NumberDeserializers.java:710 looksLikeValidNumber on wrapper-Float string coercion.
NumberDeserializers.java:815 looksLikeValidNumber on wrapper-Double string coercion.
NumberDeserializers.java:926 looksLikeValidNumber on generic java.lang.Number string coercion (float branch).
NumberDeserializers.java:1126 looksLikeValidNumber on BigDecimal string coercion.

StringNode.java:341-397: _tryParseAsInteger/Long/BigInteger/Float/Double/BigDecimal all gate on looksLikeValidNumber; reached via public asInt/asLong/asBigInteger/asFloat/asDouble/asDecimal when app reads numbers from a JsonNode/readTree result.

Still regex-based (vulnerable) in 3.1.5 and 3.1.6; replaced in 3.1.7. 2.x fixed in 2.18.11/2.21.7/2.22.3; method did not exist before 2.17.0 so 2.16.x and earlier are NOT affected.

rule_hint: FLAG when jar has tools.jackson.core:jackson-core in [3.0.0,3.1.6] or [3.2.0,3.2.1] AND app binds untrusted JSON. Reachable in DEFAULT config via any @RequestBody/readValue target that (transitively) has a float/double/BigDecimal/Number field, or any code calling JsonNode.asInt/asDouble/asDecimal on parsed untrusted input. Bytecode markers: invokestatic tools/jackson/core/io/NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber; presence of Float/Double/BigDecimal/Number-typed deserialized properties. summary: Unbounded error-token growth (CWE-770/CWE-400) in UTF8DataInputJsonParser: its _reportInvalidToken() builds the error-message token in a loop that never checks ErrorReportConfiguration.getMaxErrorTokenLength() (default 256), unlike the InputStream/Reader parsers. A malformed token on a DataInput-backed parser is copied in full into the exception message, so a ~20M-char bogus token yields a ~20M-char message and can trigger OutOfMemoryError; no StreamReadConstraints setting mitigates it.
vulnerable_feature: JSON parsing over a java.io.DataInput source only (JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput) / ObjectMapper|ObjectReader.readValue(DataInput...)), which constructs UTF8DataInputJsonParser. The InputStream and Reader parsers already enforce maxErrorTokenLength and are not affected.
trigger_conditions: App parses untrusted JSON through a DataInput source: ObjectMapper/ObjectReader.readValue(DataInput...), readTree(DataInput), createParser(DataInput). This is NOT the path Spring MVC's Jackson message converter uses (it passes InputStream or Reader - see invocation note).

Attacker sends an unrecognized/invalid token (e.g. a bare identifier like 'tru'+very long run, or any non-JSON token) whose identifier-character run is extremely long (hundreds of thousands to millions of chars).
No feature flag required; the bug is that the DataInput parser ignores the maxErrorTokenLength cap that the other parsers honor.

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Diff core 3.1.5->3.1.7 (issue #1698): the while-loop in _reportInvalidToken(int ch, String matchedPart, String msg) at 3.1.5 line 2968-2988 appends decoded chars with no bound; 3.1.7 adds 'final int maxTokenLength = _ioContext.errorReportConfiguration().getMaxErrorTokenLength();' and breaks with '...' when sb.length() >= maxTokenLength. Siblings UTF8StreamJsonParser._reportInvalidToken (desc (Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;)Ltools/jackson/core/...;) and ReaderBasedJsonParser._reportInvalidToken already had the cap in 3.1.5.
2-arg overload (3.1.5 line 2963) delegates to the 3-arg one; reached from _matchToken (line 2456) and _checkMatchEnd (line 2471) on malformed true/false/null-like tokens.
3.1.5 line 2330 calls _reportInvalidToken(c, "", _validJsonTokenList()) for an unexpected leading character; also changed in the 3.1.7 diff (multi-byte decode path).

fix_evidence.release_note: jackson-core 3.1.7 / 3.2.3: '#1698: `UTF8DataInputJsonParser` does not honor `maxErrorTokenLength` when reporting an unrecognized token [CVE-2026-89425] (fix by @pjfanning)'. Introduced in 2.8.0 per advisory. Confirmed fixed only in 3.1.7 (not 3.1.6) and 3.2.3 (not 3.2.2) by grep of getMaxErrorTokenLength in the DataInput parser across tags.
fix_evidence.diff_summary: core-UTF8DataInputJsonParser-3.1.5-3.1.7.diff: in _reportInvalidToken, add maxTokenLength lookup from errorReportConfiguration() and 'if (sb.length() >= maxTokenLength) { sb.append("..."); break; }' inside the token-collecting loop (plus unrelated multi-byte decode hardening and _growNameDecodeBuffer rename).

rule_hint: FLAG when jar has tools.jackson.core:jackson-core in [3.0.0,3.1.6] or [3.2.0,3.2.2] AND app code (or a framework) constructs a parser from a DataInput. Bytecode markers: calls to createParser/readValue/readTree whose argument type is java/io/DataInput, or 'new UTF8DataInputJsonParser'. For a plain Spring MVC JSON REST app this path is NOT reached by default (the converter uses InputStream/Reader) -> reachability LOW unless the app explicitly wraps request bodies in a DataInput/DataInputStream and calls readValue(DataInput,...). Treat as app_calls_library: requires a specific API choice, not just having @RequestBody endpoints.

summary: CPU DoS (CWE-400) when binding a JSON string to a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar field: CoreXMLDeserializers$Std._deserialize() passes the attacker string straight to DatatypeFactory.newDuration()/newXMLGregorianCalendar(), which parse numeric components with the O(n^2) BigInteger(String)/BigDecimal(String) constructors. The usual number-length limit is not applied, so a long digit run ties up a CPU thread for seconds to minutes.
vulnerable_feature: Deserialization of the two javax.xml.datatype types (Duration, XMLGregorianCalendar) from a JSON string. These deserializers are registered by default (OptionalHandlerFactory -> CoreXMLDeserializers) with no opt-in, whenever such a field/type is present in the target graph and the javax.xml.datatype classes are on the classpath.
trigger_conditions: App deserializes untrusted JSON into a type that (transitively) has a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar property, or reads those types directly (e.g. @RequestBody target contains such a field).

Attacker supplies that field as a JSON string with a very long run of digits in a numeric component, e.g. {"d":"P111...1Y"} (Duration) or an XMLGregorianCalendar lexical form with a huge fractional-seconds/year digit run.
Default config is sufficient; no polymorphism or special feature needed. (javax.xml.datatype is part of the JDK, so the deserializers are available by default.)

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Diff databind 3.1.5->3.1.6 (issue #6127): in _deserialize, before _dataTypeFactory.newDuration(value) (TYPE_DURATION) and before the newXMLGregorianCalendar path (TYPE_G_CALENDAR), 3.1.6 inserts _validateTimestampLength(ctxt, value). 3.1.5 passes value unvalidated. desc from FromStringDeserializer abstract _deserialize(String, DeserializationContext).

public entry (overrides FromStringDeserializer.deserialize) that reads the JSON string then calls _deserialize; this is what Spring's converter chain invokes for a Duration/XMLGregorianCalendar field.

fix_evidence.release_note: jackson-databind 3.1.6 / 3.2.2: '#6127: Add `StreamReadConstraints` number len constraint to `javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar` and `javax.xml.datatype.Duration` [CVE-2026-68497] (reported by @waydeshi) (fix by @pjfanning)'. Note fixed versions are 3.1.6 and 3.2.2 (one minor earlier than the other databind CVEs here). 2.x fixed in 2.18.10/2.21.6/2.22.2.
fix_evidence.diff_summary: databind-CoreXMLDeserializers-3.1.5-3.1.6.diff: adds _validateTimestampLength(ctxt, value) calls in the TYPE_DURATION and TYPE_G_CALENDAR branches of _deserialize. _validateTimestampLength is a new StdDeserializer helper (also added in 3.1.6) that throws StreamConstraintsException when value.length() > StreamReadConstraints.getMaxNumberLength() (default 1000).
fix_evidence.commit: a99b7e74c8928f43f6975773a8c862c8316178bd (2.x branch per raw path; PR #6127). 3.x fix shipped in tag jackson-databind-3.1.6 (verified _validateTimestampLength present).

rule_hint: FLAG when jar has tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind in [3.0.0,3.1.5] or 3.2.0/3.2.1 AND app binds untrusted JSON into a graph containing javax.xml.datatype.Duration or javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar. Bytecode/type markers: deserialized properties or @RequestBody targets referencing javax/xml/datatype/Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar; presence of tools.jackson.databind.ext.CoreXMLDeserializers. framework_invokes once such a field exists on a JSON endpoint; app_calls_library if the app calls readValue for those types directly - hence 'both'. If no such field/type appears anywhere in app model classes, NOT reachable.

summary: Memory-exhaustion DoS (CWE-400) via unbounded growth of the per-TypeDeserializer type-id cache. TypeDeserializerBase._findDeserializer() caches the resolved deserializer keyed by the raw, attacker-supplied type id in an unbounded ConcurrentHashMap (_deserializers). With name-based polymorphism plus a fallback (defaultImpl / problem handler), each distinct unknown id becomes its own permanent cache entry on a long-lived ObjectMapper, so a stream of unique ids grows the heap until OOM.
vulnerable_feature: Polymorphic deserialization with @JsonTypeInfo where unrecognized type ids resolve to a fallback instead of failing: Id.NAME (or Id.CLASS/MINIMAL_CLASS) with a defaultImpl, or a custom DeserializationProblemHandler.handleUnknownTypeId, combined with a reused (long-lived) ObjectMapper/JsonMapper.
trigger_conditions: App enables polymorphic typing on a deserialized type: @JsonTypeInfo(use=Id.NAME/Id.CLASS/..., defaultImpl=...) on a base type reachable from untrusted JSON, OR a registered DeserializationProblemHandler that maps unknown ids to a type, OR activateDefaultTyping with a permissive validator.
Unrecognized type ids must NOT hard-fail: a defaultImpl or problem handler must exist (with plain FAIL_ON_INVALID_SUBTYPE=true default and no defaultImpl, an unknown id throws and nothing is cached).
The ObjectMapper/JsonMapper is shared and long-lived (Spring's default singleton is), and the attacker sends many requests each with a distinct unknown type id.

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Diff databind 3.1.5->3.1.7 (issue #6203): 3.1.5 unconditionally does _deserializers.put(typeId, deser) (line 200) with no size/length bound; 3.1.7 adds MAX_CACHED_TYPE_IDS=1000 and MAX_CACHED_TYPE_ID_LENGTH=256, returns early (no caching) for the unknown-id/NullifyingDeserializer fallback, and clears the map when full. desc from source signature '_findDeserializer(DeserializationContext ctxt, String typeId)' returning ValueDeserializer<Object>.

AsPropertyTypeDeserializer.java:119 calls _findDeserializer(ctxt, typeId) with the attacker-supplied id; this is the common As.PROPERTY inclusion path. AsArrayTypeDeserializer._deserialize (line 92) and AsWrapperTypeDeserializer._deserialize (line 98) are the other call sites.

fix_evidence.release_note: jackson-databind 3.1.7 / 3.2.3: '#6203: Prevent unbounded growth of type id cache in `TypeDeserializer` [CVE-2026-91776] (reported by @dabirt) (fix by @pjfanning)'. 2.x fixed in 2.18.11/2.21.7/2.22.3. Confirmed MAX_CACHED_TYPE_IDS absent in 3.2.2, present in 3.2.3.
fix_evidence.diff_summary: databind-TypeDeserializerBase-3.1.5-3.1.7.diff: adds constants MAX_CACHED_TYPE_IDS=1000 and MAX_CACHED_TYPE_ID_LENGTH=256; for unknown ids resolved via problem handler returns findContextualValueDeserializer(...) WITHOUT caching; returns the NullifyingDeserializer fallback without caching; and before _deserializers.put, skips caching if typeId.length()>256 and clears the map if size>=1000.

rule_hint: FLAG when jar has tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind in [3.0.0,3.1.6] or [3.2.0,3.2.2] AND app uses fallback polymorphic typing on untrusted input. Markers: @JsonTypeInfo with a defaultImpl attribute (use=NAME/CLASS/MINIMAL_CLASS) on types reachable from @RequestBody; activateDefaultTyping(...) calls; registered DeserializationProblemHandler (addHandler). A plain app with NO @JsonTypeInfo/defaultImpl and no default typing is NOT reachable (default_config_affected=false). Spring MVC does not enable default typing on its own, so reachability depends on app model annotations/config -> 'both'. PoC on real Jackson 2.16.1 confirmed 10,000 distinct unknown ids -> 10,000 retained cache entries with @JsonTypeInfo(use=NAME, defaultImpl=...).

summary: Quadratic-complexity CPU DoS (CWE-400) in @JsonIdentityInfo forward-reference completion for Collection and Map deserializers. Unresolved object-id references are kept in an ArrayList and each resolution does a linear scan plus addAll merge; when N references are created and then their ids are defined in reverse order, completion costs O(N^2) (reporter measured ~2,003,000 ID comparisons at N=2000).
vulnerable_feature: Deserialization of JSON into a Collection or Map whose element/value type uses @JsonIdentityInfo (object identity), where the payload contains many forward references (ids used before they are defined).
trigger_conditions: App deserializes untrusted JSON into an @JsonIdentityInfo-enabled collection or map (element/value type annotated with @JsonIdentityInfo, or a List/Map field of such a type reachable from @RequestBody).
Attacker sends N forward references (object ids referenced before definition) in the collection/map and then defines those same ids, especially in reverse order, to force the worst-case scan.
Requires @JsonIdentityInfo usage; no deep nesting or special JSON syntax, no auth if the endpoint is public. StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength (unset by default) would cap payload size.

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Diff databind 3.1.5->3.1.7 (issue #6204): 3.1.5 resolveForwardReference iterates the whole _accumulator List each call (Iterator + previous.addAll(ref.next)) -> O(N^2); 3.1.7 replaces it with a keyed _unresolvedById map (Deque per id) and a _pending/_pendingStart structure that moves each value once. desc from source signature resolveForwardReference(DeserializationContext, Object id, Object value).
Diff databind 3.1.5->3.1.7 (issue #6204): identical quadratic scan+putAll pattern in the Map accumulator, replaced by the same _unresolvedById/_pending approach.

CollectionDeserializer.java:480 - reached only when _valueDeserializer.getObjectIdReader(ctxt) != null (i.e. element type has @JsonIdentityInfo); it builds the CollectionReferringAccumulator and drives handleUnresolvedReference/resolve. Entry from _deserializeFromArray (line 376 branch).
MapDeserializer.java:489 - useObjectId = getObjectIdReader(ctxt)!=null gates creation of MapReferringAccumulator; also _readAndBindStringKeyMap (line 570).

fix_evidence.release_note: jackson-databind 3.1.7 / 3.2.3: '#6204: Avoid quadratic forward-reference resolution in Collection/Map deserializers [CVE-2026-91777] (reported by @dabirt) (fix by @pjfanning)'. Sibling '#6205: Avoid quadratic forward-reference resolution in `ObjectArrayDeserializer`' (array variant, no separate CVE) in the same release. 2.x fixed 2.18.11/2.21.7/2.22.3. Confirmed _unresolvedById absent in 3.2.2, present in 3.2.3.
fix_evidence.diff_summary: databind-CollectionDeserializer / MapDeserializer 3.1.5->3.1.7 diffs: replace the single _accumulator ArrayList + full-scan resolveForwardReference (previous.addAll(ref.next)) with (a) _pending list + _pendingStart index that moves each value once, and (b) _unresolvedById Map<Object,Deque<Referring>> for O(1) id lookup. CollectionReferring/MapReferring lose the 'next' buffer and gain resolve()/isResolved()/resolvedValue().

rule_hint: FLAG when jar has tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind in [3.0.0,3.1.6] or [3.2.0,3.2.2] AND app model uses @JsonIdentityInfo on a type held in a List/Map reachable from untrusted JSON. Markers: @JsonIdentityInfo annotations on classes used as collection elements/map values; deserialization into Collection/Map of such types. Note the O(N^2) path only runs when getObjectIdReader != null (object-id active); a plain collection without @JsonIdentityInfo is NOT affected (default_config_affected=false). Spring MVC reaches it only if app model opts into object ids -> 'both'. PoC on real Jackson 2.16.1 (@JsonIdentityInfo List): reverse-order defs N=8000/16000/32000 = 683/3422/13798 ms vs forward-order 28/36/56 ms (clear quadratic).

summary: The java.nio.file.Path deserializer passes an attacker-supplied string to new URI(value) and Path.of(uri), and on FileSystemNotFoundException walks ServiceLoader<FileSystemProvider> and calls getPath on the provider for the attacker-chosen scheme. Untrusted JSON can drive any registered FileSystemProvider during readValue. With only JDK providers the result is inert.
vulnerable_feature: Deserializing java.nio.file.Path values from untrusted JSON
trigger_conditions: a deserialized type has a java.nio.file.Path field (or Path is read directly)
fix_evidence: Commits ce26eda3 / d94bb632 (3.x): JDKFromStringDeserializer.findDeserializer returns a new NioPathDeserializer that only allows the 'file' scheme by default; NioPathHelper is removed. Commit cc6756b6 (2.x): ext.NioPathDeserializer restricted the same way.

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Removed by the fix. javap on 3.1.5.

rule_hint: Same shape as CVE-2026-89407: a Path field in a type reachable from a deserialization root.

summary: DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator, the validator used for @JsonTypeInfo without a custom PolymorphicTypeValidator, did not treat java.lang.Comparable as an unsafe base type, so a @JsonTypeInfo property typed Comparable accepts almost any class (e.g. java.io.File with an attacker-chosen path). Global default typing is not affected (it requires an explicit validator).
vulnerable_feature: @JsonTypeInfo with base type java.lang.Comparable and no custom PolymorphicTypeValidator
trigger_conditions: the polymorphic base type is Comparable (field or class)
fix_evidence: Commit eb3b7fc0 (2.x): DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator.isUnsafeBaseType adds Comparable. The 3.x fix (3.1.6) is in the same class; the 3.x commit was not fetched, the 3.1.5 signatures were checked with javap.

vulnerable_methods.evidence: Missing Comparable. javap on 3.1.5; 3.x fix commit not fetched.
Returns true for every base type outside the unsafe set. javap on 3.1.5.

rule_hint: Rule: unreachable without any @JsonTypeInfo; with @JsonTypeInfo, reachable when a deserialized type has a Comparable field, otherwise a human checks the base types.
